feedback.observed: The generic frontend-design skill kept being activated even after project-specific motion research had been completed and preserved, adding context without improving the direction.
feedback.expected: Use the preserved green-movement shot contract and measured 700px frames as the motion authority; return to external or generic design guidance only when the project evidence has a named gap.
feedback.evidence: The Obsidian study now contains sourced staging, continuity, typography, timing, rejection, and Gate rules specific to this SVG, while the generic skill contributed no uncovered job in the latest pass.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect the active capability routing and the next motion candidate; frontend-design must not activate, and each motion decision must map to the project shot contract or a measured source defect.

feedback.observed: Several successive turnover fixes improved empty time, endpoint distance, footprint clearance, and bridge speed, but the user still had to identify that the continuous carrier path communicated the wrong identity story.
feedback.expected: For an identity or continuity complaint, inspect the actor lifecycle and adjacent rendered frames before optimizing another coordinate metric; test what story the uninterrupted trajectory communicates.
feedback.evidence: V21, v25, and v26 passed their numeric turnover checks, yet the v26 source still reused one field-slot actor and moved the UFO directly from the outgoing pickup to the incoming drop. The first diagnosis that traced both facts produced the bounded service-cut correction.
feedback.reproduction: For the next actor-identity motion report, require a source lifecycle trace plus pickup-to-next-action frame sequence before proposing a spatial or timing change.

feedback.observed: V31 still felt inconsistent, a newly delivered sheep could appear to slide in from outside its landing point, and turnover could read as the same collected sheep being moved and dropped again. Repeated still-image inspection had not isolated the structural cause.
feedback.expected: Use one perceptual rhythm for every UFO leg, give each incoming roster identity a genuinely separate field actor, materialize it only at the exact drop, and keep it fixed until the departing UFO body is hidden.
feedback.evidence: Source lifecycle tracing found that one SVG root per field slot was reused by roster identities 0, 6, 12, and later; hidden actors were parked at -9999px; incoming bridge movement began at UFO departure rather than after body disappearance; and shared percentage phases produced different playback durations across entry, deployment, turnover, convergence, and exit.
feedback.reproduction: Trace every roster actor from first visibility at both 30fps and 120fps, inspect adjacent 700px entry/deployment/turnover/collection/convergence/exit frames, and reject actor reuse, any offscreen transform, an unstable first reveal, mixed UFO leg timing, or incoming movement before the departing body is hidden.

proposals.change_target: shared UFO blink timing, roster field-actor lifecycle, exact-drop hold timing, deterministic SVG assertions, browser first-reveal probes, and durable behavior guidance
proposals.cause: V31 reused one animated SVG root for every later identity occupying a field slot, parked hidden sheep offscreen, began the incoming bridge while the carrier was still visibly departing, and expressed shared UFO phases as percentages of unequal leg durations.
proposals.candidate_change: Render one lifecycle actor per roster identity while reusing the existing slot route animation, remove all offscreen sheep coordinates, anchor each first visible transform to its exact drop, delay movement until the departing UFO body is hidden, and route entry, deployment, turnover, collection, finale convergence, and exit through one fixed 0.14-source-second / 0.182-playback-second blink with at most 8px of visible body travel at each edge and the existing compact green light plus streak in the middle.
proposals.discovery_evidence: The local candidate contains 28 unique roster actors and no -9999px transform. Fresh 30fps and 120fps browser probes report zero outside or unstable first-reveal failures across all 28 identities. Adjacent 700px frames show the incoming sheep fixed at its exact drop until the carrier body is hidden and one 0.182-second UFO rhythm across every named leg.
proposals.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture and npm run check; probe every roster actor's first visible coordinate at 30fps and 120fps; inspect fresh 700px forced-theme adjacent frames for entry, deployments, first/later/final turnover, collection, convergence, exit, reduced motion, roster density, finale, and terminal state.
proposals.primary_metric: All roster identities own independent exact-drop lifecycles with zero offscreen or unstable first reveals, and every UFO leg uses the same fixed playback rhythm without cross-field body exposure.
proposals.prediction: Fixing actor ownership and timing in their shared render and blink paths will remove the outside-slide and same-sheep story more reliably than another per-scene opacity or coordinate patch.
proposals.falsification_condition: Reject if any roster identity reuses another identity's DOM actor, any hidden sheep uses an offscreen coordinate, a first visible frame is outside or moving into its drop, a sheep moves before the departing UFO body is hidden, UFO legs use different playback rhythms, body travel crosses the middle, accepted causal/layout/finale behavior regresses, runtime exceeds 50 seconds, or npm run check fails.
proposals.regression_check: npm run check plus a fresh independent exact-time 700px Gate across lifecycle, 30fps and 120fps first reveals, themes, reduced motion, roster densities, finale, terminal state, size, and runtime.
proposals.transfer_check: Not applicable; this is a project-scoped actor-lifecycle and motion correction.
